title: Bitcoin Tops $80,000 for First Time Since May as Dollar Weakens on Treasury Buyback Plans
excerpt: The cryptocurrency has rallied 28% in August, its best month since November 2024, as investors pile into the debasement trade amid growing U.S. fiscal concerns.
body:
• Bitcoin surged past $80,000 on Tuesday for the first time since mid-May, reaching $81,237 as the U.S. dollar weakened following Treasury bond buyback plans.
  • The cryptocurrency has risen 28% in August, its strongest monthly gain since November 2024, now outperforming both gold and the S&P 500 over six months.
  • The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) attracted $1 billion in inflows last week, with Friday marking its biggest single-day inflow since January.
  • Analysts say the Treasury's decision to double long-bond buybacks has fueled the so-called debasement trade, shifting pressure from bonds to the dollar and benefiting hard assets.

Bitcoin crossed $80,000 on Tuesday to hit a three-month high, driven by a weakening U.S. dollar and growing investor conviction that Washington will prioritize keeping long-term bond yields in check — even at the currency's expense.

The world's largest cryptocurrency touched $81,237.94 in Asian trading hours before settling around $80,323, according to CoinDesk data. The move extends a 28% rally in August that puts bitcoin on track for its strongest monthly performance since November 2024, when it surged following the U.S. presidential election.

Treasury Buybacks Ignite the Debasement Trade

The catalyst arrived on August 19, when the U.S. Treasury announced plans to at least double its buybacks of longer-dated government bonds starting September 9. While the program is officially intended to support market liquidity, traders interpreted it as a signal that policymakers have limited tolerance for further increases in long-end yields — particularly against the backdrop of $40 trillion in U.S. government debt.

"Treasury changed the market conversation even if it did not change monetary policy. Traders now know Washington is prepared to respond when the long end becomes sufficiently uncomfortable."

— Stephen Innes, Global Strategist, Quintex Intel

The announcement stoked what analysts call the debasement trade: the idea that government intervention to suppress bond yields ultimately shifts the pressure onto the currency, eroding purchasing power and making hard assets like bitcoin and gold more attractive.

ETF Inflows Signal Institutional Momentum

Institutional appetite has been visible in the spot bitcoin ETF market. The iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT), the largest fund tracking bitcoin prices, attracted roughly $1 billion in net inflows last week, with Friday alone seeing $503 million — its biggest single-day haul since January, according to FactSet data. The fund surged nearly 23% last week and gained another 2% in overnight trading Tuesday.

Bitcoin is now outperforming both gold and U.S. equities as measured by the S&P 500 over a rolling six-month period, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Exchange-traded funds have made it easier for conventional investors to express the debasement narrative, with bitcoin becoming what Innes described as the "higher beta sibling" of gold for the same macro trade.

Crypto Legislation Adds Tailwind

The rally has drawn additional fuel from Washington. President Donald Trump last week called on Congress to pass legislation that would bring clearer regulatory definitions to the cryptocurrency sector. Since that push, bitcoin has gained 16%.

"This is exactly the type of thing bitcoin loves. Bitcoin was built to allow investors a way to avoid this type of intervention."

— Geoff Kendrick, Global Head of Digital Assets Research, Standard Chartered

What Comes Next

Despite the August surge, bitcoin remains in the red for 2026 overall. Both bitcoin and gold have entered overbought territory on the 14-day relative strength index, a technical indicator that readings above 70 suggest stretched positioning. Gold, which has risen over 14% this month alone, edged slightly lower on Tuesday.

The near-term test for the rally will be whether the dollar continues to weaken and whether Treasury yields stabilize. Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, said Secretary Bessent's messaging has reinforced the view that policymakers will maintain a supportive macro backdrop for assets like bitcoin and gold at least through the midterm elections. Whether that backdrop holds beyond the political cycle remains the open question.
